subject: Mercury4b elevated 5xx / timeouts — incident update and follow-up
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Atlas AI Support <support@atlasai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2029 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Mercury4b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notice

Hi Rebecca / Atlas team,

Quick note to let you know we observed an elevated rate of 5xx and request timeouts for the Mercury4b model serving your production route (region: us-west-2) starting ~08:50 PDT. The issue affected ~12% of requests for a ~25 minute window and manifested as 503/504 responses or stalled streaming.

What we did immediately:
- Degraded traffic away from the impacted shard to a warm fallback variant (mercury4b-stable-quant) to keep your app serving.
- Scoped the fault to a subset of NVMe-backed inference nodes (instance pool m-inf-8) — ops has isolated the nodes and collected logs.
- Enabled additional autoscaling capacity for your dedicated pool and temporarily increased concurrency caps to reduce queuing.

Impact for Atlas AI: short bursts of failed responses and slightly elevated tail latency for streaming sessions during the window. No data exposure.

Next steps (we are doing these now):
1) Ops will finish a root-cause triage and upload logs/snippets.
2) We'll continue routing your traffic to the fallback variant and monitor for errors.
3) Expect a follow-up within 2–3 hours with technical findings and mitigation timeline.

Attachments: [Attachment: mercury4b-503-ops-log-snippet.txt (text/plain)]

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your users. I'll keep you posted as soon as we have a concrete RCA and ETA for returning full traffic to Mercury4b.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Atlas AI Support <support@atlasai.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2029 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Mercury4b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notice

On Sat, Jun 15, 2029 at 09:05 Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick note to let you know we observed an elevated rate of 5xx and request timeouts for the Mercury4b model serving your production route (region: us-west-2) starting ~08:50 PDT.

Folks — summarizing Ops findings so far:
- Root cause (preliminary): one NVMe controller on shard-12 experienced intermittent write stalls under peak KV cache churn. That caused the local inference process to stall when attempting to checkpoint or persist transient cache pages, manifesting as request-level timeouts and hard 5xx from the serving layer.
- Why only Mercury4b: Mercury uses a heavy prefix-KV caching strategy with larger checkpoint windows; the particular shard had an older firmware revision and slightly lower spare-block reserve which amplified the stall.
- Mitigation taken: traffic migration to mercury4b-stable-quant + per-instance restart on the affected pool. Firmware upgrade planned for the node group during the maintenance window.

We attached an ops log snippet and a quick cache-eviction graph that shows the correlation between KV eviction spikes and 503 counts.

Immediate ask for Atlas: confirm if you noticed any correlated errors on your side (specific request IDs are in the snippet). We'll also provide a rolling timeline for reintroducing Mercury4b with staged canary routing.

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mercury4b-cache-eviction-graph.png (image/png)]
From: Rebecca Johnson <rebecca.johnson@atlasai.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2029 12:43:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Mercury4b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notice

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks for the quick update and for routing us to the fallback. We did see an uptick in 5xx in our monitoring and a handful of user-facing session failures between 08:48–09:20 PDT. The request IDs in your snippet match logs we pulled.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether this will affect our SLA credits for June? We need a written summary we can share with procurement.
2) Please provide the ETA for returning to Mercury4b full traffic and what safeguards will be added so this doesn’t recur (we rely on Mercury for a low-latency routing for chat features).

Also, we’d like to join the postmortem call if you schedule one. Please loop in their engineering lead as needed.

—Rebecca
Head of Platform, Atlas AI
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Johnson <rebecca.johnson@atlasai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2029 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Mercury4b elevated 5xx/timeouts — incident resolution & follow-up plan

Rebecca — thanks for the confirmation and the ask. Final update for today and next steps: 

Resolution summary:
- We completed a targeted restart and removed the affected NVMe nodes from the active pool; the error rate returned to baseline by 14:52 PDT after traffic fully drained from the impacted shard.
- We verified request replays against the fallback variant and validated no data corruption.

Planned mitigations and timeline:
1) Firmware and spare-block remediation for the NVMe devices in shard-12 — scheduled for maintenance window Tue 2029-06-18 02:00–04:00 PDT. (low-risk, non-disruptive; anticipates a 60-minute window for node cycling)
2) Canary reintroduction of Mercury4b on a single shard with elevated telemetry + automatic rollback on 5xx spike — Wed 2029-06-19 09:00 PDT. We'll keep initial traffic <5% and hold for 2 hours of stable signals before increasing.
3) Long-term: add a heuristic to detect NVMe checkpoint stalls earlier (instrument KV write latency) and a defensive fallback to stream-only mode when checkpoint backpressure is detected. Target Q3 milestone.

SLA / credits: We will record this incident per our SLA policy and open a credit request for the impacted minutes. I'll follow up with formal credit accounting and include a brief incident narrative you can share with procurement.

Postmortem and invite:
- We're scheduling a 60-minute postmortem review for Thu 2029-06-20 10:00 PDT. I’ll send the calendar invite with a read-ahead (playbook + ops logs). Please confirm attendees; we’ll include our engineering lead (Rishi) and product owner (Marissa).

Attachments: [Attachment: incident-playbook-mercury4b.pdf]

Apologies again for the interruption — we prioritize preventing recurrences and will share the final RCA after the postmortem.

Best,
Olga
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
